description: Lebanese Red Lentil Soup, known as Adas, is a comforting and nutritious staple in Middle Eastern cuisine. This hearty vegan soup is packed with the earthy flavor of red lentils, brightened by lemon, and aromatic with garlic and cumin. It is a perfect one-pot meal, easy to prepare and loved by all.

instructions.title: Prepare the Lentils and Aromatics
instructions.text: Rinse the red lentils thoroughly under cold water until the water runs clear; drain well. In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and diced carrot, cooking until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Add Spices and Tomato Paste
instructions.text: Stir in the tomato paste, ground cumin, ground coriander, and turmeric powder. Cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, to toast the spices and deepen their flavor. This step is crucial for building the soup's aromatic base.

instructions.title: Combine Lentils and Broth
instructions.text: Add the rinsed red lentils to the pot, stirring to combine them with the aromatics and spices. Pour in the vegetable broth and bring the mixture to a boil. Once boiling, reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let it simmer.

instructions.title: Simmer to Perfection
instructions.text: Allow the soup to simmer gently for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are very tender and have broken down, creating a thick, creamy texture. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking to the bottom of the pot. If the soup becomes too thick, you can add a little more broth or water.

instructions.title: Season and Finish with Lemon
instructions.text: Remove the pot from the heat. Stir in the fresh lemon juice, then season generously with salt and black pepper to taste. The lemon juice is key to the authentic Lebanese flavor, so do not skip it. Taste and adjust seasonings as needed.

instructions.title: Serve Hot
instructions.text: Ladle the hot Lebanese Red Lentil Soup (Adas) into bowls. Garnish each serving with a sprinkle of fresh chopped cilantro. Serve immediately with warm pita bread or a side of fresh vegetables for dipping. Enjoy this comforting and wholesome Middle Eastern delight.

tips: For an extra layer of flavor, consider adding a pinch of dried mint along with the spices. This is a common addition in some regional variations.

Do not overcook the lentils to the point of being mushy; they should be soft and creamy but still hold some texture. If you prefer a smoother soup, you can use an immersion blender to partially puree it.
Always taste and adjust the lemon and salt at the end. The brightness of fresh lemon juice truly elevates the earthy flavors of the lentils.
article:
Discovering the rich tapestry of Middle Eastern cuisine often leads to delightful surprises, and few dishes offer the comforting embrace of a warm bowl of soup quite like Lebanese Red Lentil Soup, known locally as Adas. This simple yet profoundly flavorful dish is a cornerstone of Lebanese home cooking, cherished for its nourishing qualities, ease of preparation, and budget-friendly ingredients. It’s a testament to how humble components can come together to create something truly extraordinary – a bright, zesty, and deeply satisfying meal that transcends cultural boundaries.

Whether you're seeking a hearty weeknight dinner, a wholesome lunch, or a soothing remedy on a cold day, Adas delivers. It's naturally vegan, gluten-free, and packed with plant-based protein and fiber, making it an ideal choice for health-conscious eaters and those following specific dietary paths. Join us as we explore the magic of this beloved Middle Eastern soup, from its essential ingredients to expert tips for perfecting your own pot of this liquid gold.

## What is Lebanese Red Lentil Soup (Adas)?

Lebanese Red Lentil Soup, or Adas, is a classic Middle Eastern staple, particularly revered in Lebanon. It’s a vibrant, golden-hued soup characterized by its smooth texture, often achieved by blending the cooked lentils, and its distinctively bright, tangy flavor profile, primarily from generous amounts of fresh lemon juice. Unlike some other lentil soups that might rely heavily on a complex array of spices or meats, Adas celebrates the simplicity and inherent goodness of its core ingredients.

At its heart, Adas is made from red lentils, which cook down quickly into a creamy consistency, onions, garlic, and a few key spices like cumin. What truly sets the Lebanese version apart is the prominent role of lemon, which cuts through the richness of the lentils and adds a refreshing zest. Often, a "tasha" – a sizzling sauté of garlic and fresh mint in olive oil – is prepared and stirred into or drizzled over the finished soup, adding an aromatic flourish and an extra layer of flavor. This soup is more than just a meal; it's a symbol of warmth, hospitality, and the nourishing power of simple, wholesome food in Lebanese culture. It’s a common sight on family tables, particularly during the cooler months or as a light, yet fulfilling, meal during the fasting month of Ramadan.

## Ingredients You'll Need for Adas Soup

Creating an authentic Lebanese Red Lentil Soup doesn't require a long list of exotic ingredients. In fact, its beauty lies in its simplicity. Here’s what you’ll need to gather:

*   **Red Lentils:** The star of the show! Make sure they are split red lentils, as they cook faster and break down more easily for a creamy soup.
*   **Onions:** One large yellow onion, finely chopped, forms the aromatic base.
*   **Garlic:** Several cloves, minced, provide depth of flavor.
*   **Olive Oil:** A good quality extra virgin olive oil is essential for sautéing and for drizzling over the finished soup.
*   **Vegetable Broth or Water:** While water works perfectly fine, vegetable broth will add an extra layer of savoriness.
*   **Fresh Lemon Juice:** This is non-negotiable! You'll need the juice of 2-3 lemons, or even more, to achieve that signature tangy brightness.
*   **Cumin:** Ground cumin is the primary spice, imparting earthy warmth.
*   **Salt & Black Pepper:** To taste, enhancing all the other flavors.
*   **Optional for Garnish/Flavor:** Fresh mint leaves (chopped), fresh parsley (chopped), and a pinch of dried mint for the optional "tasha" (garlic-mint sizzle).

## How to Make Lebanese Red Lentil Soup: Step-by-Step

Preparing this comforting Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is remarkably straightforward. Follow these steps for a perfect bowl every time:

1.  **Rinse the Lentils:** Place your red lentils in a fine-mesh sieve and rinse them thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear. This removes any dust or debris. Set aside.
2.  **Sauté Aromatics:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat about 2-3 tablespoons of olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and sauté until they are soft and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant, being careful not to burn it.
3.  **Combine Ingredients:** Add the rinsed lentils to the pot along with the vegetable broth (or water) and ground cumin. Bring the mixture to a boil.
4.  **Simmer and Cook:** Once boiling, reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let it simmer for about 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are very tender and have broken down. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
5.  **Blend (Optional):** For a smoother, creamier consistency, use an immersion blender to blend the soup directly in the pot until it reaches your desired texture. Alternatively, you can carefully transfer batches to a regular blender (vent the lid!) and blend until smooth, then return to the pot. If you prefer a more rustic texture, you can mash some of the lentils with the back of a spoon.
6.  **Season and Finish:** Stir in the fresh lemon juice. Start with the juice of two lemons and add more to taste. Season generously with salt and black pepper. Taste and adjust seasonings as needed – the lemon should be bright and noticeable. If the soup is too thick, add a little more hot water or broth to reach your preferred consistency.
7.  **Prepare the Tasha (Optional but Recommended):** In a small pan, heat a tablespoon of olive oil over medium heat. Add 1-2 minced garlic cloves and a teaspoon of dried mint (or a tablespoon of fresh chopped mint). Sauté for about 30 seconds until fragrant. Immediately pour this sizzling mixture into the hot soup and stir it in, or ladle the soup into bowls and drizzle the tasha over each serving.

## Pro Tips for the Best Lebanese Lentil Soup

While Adas is simple, a few expert tips can elevate your homemade Lebanese Red Lentil Soup from good to truly unforgettable:

*   **Don't Skip the Rinse:** Rinsing the lentils isn't just about cleanliness; it can also help reduce flatulence and improve the soup's clarity.
*   **Embrace the Lemon:** The defining characteristic of Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is its vibrant lemon flavor. Don't be shy with the lemon juice. It should be bright and tangy. Add it at the end to preserve its fresh taste.
*   **Quality Olive Oil:** Use a good extra virgin olive oil, not just for sautéing but also for a final drizzle over each serving. It adds a wonderful richness and aroma.
*   **Blend for Creaminess:** While some prefer a chunkier soup, blending it (either partially or fully) creates that signature smooth, velvety texture that most Lebanese families aim for. An immersion blender makes this incredibly easy.
*   **The Tasha is Key:** That optional garlic-mint sizzle (tasha) adds an incredible layer of aromatic complexity. It’s a small step that makes a big difference in authentic flavor.
*   **Adjust Consistency:** Red lentils absorb a lot of liquid. If your soup thickens too much upon standing, simply thin it out with a little hot water or vegetable broth until it reaches your desired consistency.

## Serving Suggestions & Pairings

Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is a wonderfully versatile dish that can be enjoyed in many ways. It’s often served as a main course for a light meal, especially when paired with fresh bread.

*   **Pita Bread:** The ultimate companion! Warm pita bread is perfect for scooping up every last drop of the creamy soup.
*   **Crusty Bread:** A good rustic loaf of crusty bread also works beautifully.
*   **Garnish Generously:** Always serve with a fresh drizzle of extra virgin olive oil, a sprinkle of fresh chopped mint or parsley, and extra lemon wedges on the side for those who desire more tang.
*   **Alongside Salads:** For a complete and wholesome meal, pair Adas with a fresh, crisp salad like a simple garden salad, fattoush, or tabouleh. The freshness of the salad complements the warmth of the soup perfectly.
*   **As a Starter:** It can also serve as a delightful and nourishing starter course for a larger Middle Eastern feast.

## Variations & Dietary Adaptations

One of the great things about Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is its inherent flexibility and suitability for various dietary needs:

*   **Naturally Vegan & Gluten-Free:** Adas is naturally vegan and gluten-free, making it an excellent choice for almost anyone. Just ensure your vegetable broth is gluten-free if you're using it.
*   **Spice It Up:** While cumin is traditional, you can experiment with a pinch of turmeric for extra color and a subtle earthy note, or a tiny dash of cayenne pepper if you like a little heat.
*   **Add Vegetables:** While classic Adas is simple, you can certainly add finely diced carrots or celery along with the onions for extra nutrients and flavor. Potatoes, diced small, can also be added for a heartier soup.
*   **Herb Variations:** Beyond mint, a little fresh cilantro or parsley can be added to the soup itself during the last few minutes of cooking, or as a garnish.
*   **Smoky Flavor:** For a subtle smoky depth, you could add a pinch of smoked paprika along with the cumin.

Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is more than just a recipe; it's an invitation to experience the warmth and generosity of Lebanese culinary tradition. Its simplicity belies a complexity of flavor that is both deeply satisfying and incredibly comforting. Whether you're a seasoned chef or a novice in the kitchen, this accessible and nutritious Middle Eastern soup is a dish you'll undoubtedly want to add to your repertoire. So, gather your ingredients, follow these steps, and prepare to be enchanted by the humble, yet magnificent, Adas.
